subject: Contract redlines: capacity unit definitions + credit ladder for Dedicated GPU pool
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@crestwellhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Contract redlines: Dedicated GPU pool - definitions & credit ladder

Marissa — attaching our redlines on the Dedicated contract. Two high-level asks: 1) we need a clear, measurable definition of a 'capacity unit' so our procurement team can map usage to the reserved commit; 2) we want a service-credit ladder tied to throughput shortfalls (examples below).

Key asks from Crestwell Procurement:  
- Define Capacity Unit: we currently propose "capacity unit = 1 GPU vRAM-hour at 32GB vRAM equivalence" (we listed conversion examples for 16GB, 24GB instances in the attachment).
- Throughput guarantee: a minimum of 75% of committed throughput (tokens/sec sustained) with monthly measurement.
- Service credit ladder: 10% credit for 1-3% monthly throughput shortfall, 25% for 3-10% shortfall, 50% for >10% shortfall. No cap was proposed.

We also flagged ambiguity around burst capacity vs baseline: the contract ties 'throughput' to the GPU pool but doesn't say how burst requests are counted or how KV cache hits factor into token accounting. Please review and propose language.

Attachments: Crestwell_Redline_v3.docx; SLA_Definitions.xlsx

Thanks,
Sara Lin
Head of Procurement, Crestwell Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@crestwellhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract redlines: Dedicated GPU pool - definitions & credit ladder

Sara — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. We can get you measurable definitions and a workable credit ladder, but a few clarifications so we propose a mutually practical clause:  

1) When you say 'sustained throughput (tokens/sec)', is Crestwell measuring at p50 or p95 window? Our billing/monitoring typically reports median and 95th percentile over 1-minute windows.  
2) For burst traffic, do you expect bursts to draw down the reserved commit, or should bursts be treated as meter-through and billed at on-demand rates?

Proposed near-term step: quick call Monday to confirm the measurement windows and an example month from your telemetry so we can run the math and show concrete credit amounts. Tentative time for us: Mon 30 Nov, 10:00am PT. If that works, we will send an updated redline with: (a) a clear capacity unit definition with conversion table, (b) a cap on monthly credits as percent of invoice, and (c) a worked example for a 12-month reserved commit.

Link: Mutual_Action_Plan: https://drive.google.com/example/mutual-action-plan (attached as stub)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Contract redlines: Dedicated GPU pool - definitions & credit ladder

Team — forwarding Crestwell's redlines (attached). They asked for a capacity unit definition and want an un-capped credit ladder. My initial thinking: we can accept a credit ladder but must cap credits at a reasonable % of the monthly invoice (legal prefers 30%). Also we should translate capacity units into our "capacity unit" abstraction (vram-hour equivalent) and include examples for 16/24/32GB GPUs.

Questions for you:  
- Ben: what delta on price/discount would you need to be comfortable if we accept a 30% max credit? Could we trade a slightly higher discount for a higher cap?
- Olga: can you draft language that ties credits to measurable metrics (95th percentile sustained throughput over a 24hr rolling window) and limits cumulative credits per billing month? Also include a clause preserving our right to degrade burst throughput (and treat bursts as on-demand).
- Karthik: can you confirm our telemetry exports (token/sec, p50/p95 windows) and the sample month we can share in the call?

Attachments: Crestwell_Redline_v3.docx; SLA_Definitions.xlsx

Thanks — I scheduled a 30min sync Mon 30th 10am PT but can move.

Marissa

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract redlines: Dedicated GPU pool - definitions & credit ladder

Marissa/Ben/Karthik — drafted suggested contract language below. I kept the structure simple so it's readable in procurement redlines:  

--- Suggested language (for redline) ---
1. Definitions: 
"Capacity Unit" means one (1) GPU-vRAM hour, expressed as the equivalent of a 32 GB GPU. For GPUs with different vRAM sizes, Capacity Units shall be converted using the table in Schedule A (e.g., 16GB = 0.5 CU/hr, 24GB = 0.75 CU/hr).

2. Throughput Measurement: 
"Committed Throughput" shall be the monthly average of sustained request-processing throughput measured as tokens-per-second at the 95th percentile over 1-minute aggregation windows, reported daily and reconciled monthly. Prefix/KV cache hits shall be excluded from throughput shortfall calculations; only end-user token generation is considered.

3. Service Credits: 
If monthly Committed Throughput falls below the Committed Throughput by the following thresholds, Customer shall be eligible for the corresponding Service Credit applied as a percentage of the monthly invoice for the Dedicated service:  
- Shortfall >3% and <=10%: 25% credit on Dedicated monthly fee.
- Shortfall >10% and <=25%: 50% credit on Dedicated monthly fee.
- Shortfall >25%: 75% credit on Dedicated monthly fee.

4. Credit Cap and Limitations: 
Total Service Credits for any given billing month shall not exceed thirty percent (30%) of the Dedicated monthly charges. Service Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy with respect to throughput shortfalls and do not entitle Customer to termination for convenience.

5. Burst and On-demand Traffic: 
Requests above the Committed Throughput shall be treated as On-Demand and billed at the applicable on-demand rates. Redwood reserves the right to throttle non-critical burst traffic when sustained utilization exceeds 110% of the Committed Throughput for a rolling one-hour window.

--- end suggested language ---

Notes: I added the 95th percentile and explicit cache exclusion to prevent double-counting. Legal prefers the 30% cap on credits. Ben — if we need to move the cap, let's discuss what discount or concession we exchange.

Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@crestwellhealth.com>, Jason Park <jason.park@crestwellhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Revised redline proposal — capacity unit + service-credit compromise

Sara/Jason — thanks for hopping on the call this morning. Per discussion, attached is our revised redline that:  
- Defines Capacity Unit as GPU-vRAM hour with a conversion table (Schedule A)
- Measures Committed Throughput using 95th percentile of tokens/sec over 1-minute windows (KV/prefix cache excluded)
- Proposes a three-tier credit ladder (25% / 50% / 75%) but includes a 30% cap on total monthly credits as a hard limit
- Clarifies burst policy — requests above committed throughput billed on-demand; Redwood may throttle non-critical bursts after 1 hour sustained >110% utilization

Examples (worked scenario included in attachment): for a 12-month reserved commit at 10 CUs, a 12% shortfall in a given month would yield a 50% credit on that month's Dedicated fee, but the credit amount will be capped to 30% of the monthly invoice under the cap rule. As discussed, we are willing to offer a 10% monthly commit discount in exchange for the 12-month commit and the 30% cap being acceptable to Crestwell.

Next steps: if Crestwell is comfortable with the language we can convert to DocuSign (link below). If you need the credit cap to move higher, please propose a concrete counter-offer (e.g., 35% cap in exchange for X concession).

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/example-doc/CST-4821-sla
Attachments: Revised_Redline_v4.docx; SLA_Definitions_Examples.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@crestwellhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Park <jason.park@crestwellhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Revised redline proposal — capacity unit + service-credit compromise

Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the worked example. Crestwell is generally supportive of the proposed measurement approach and the conversion table. Two remaining asks before we can sign: 

1) Credit cap: Crestwell requests a 40% monthly credit cap for Severity 1 incidents that impact >50% of requests for more than 2 consecutive hours. For other shortfall categories we can accept a 30% cap.
2) Burst carve-out: we need a small carve-out that allows emergency burst capacity for our clinical workflows (up to 20% above committed throughput for up to 30 minutes per day) that does not incur on-demand billing. This is for short patient-facing surges.

If Redwood can accept the Severity 1 40% cap and the emergency burst carve-out, we can sign the redline and proceed to DocuSign. Otherwise please specify the concession you would need for those ask(s).

Thanks — will await your updated language.

Regards,
Sara Lin
Head of Procurement, Crestwell Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Nov 2026 11:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Crestwell accepts with two asks (40% S1 cap + emergency burst carve-out) — internal decision

Team — Crestwell responded. They accept the overall approach but want: (A) a 40% cap for Severity 1 incidents meeting the >50%/2hr criteria, and (B) an emergency burst carve-out: up to 20% above committed throughput for up to 30 minutes/day excluded from on-demand billing.  

My read: we can accept the emergency burst carve-out with guardrails (must be pre-authorized, logged via our telemetry, and limited to non-fraud traffic). The 40% S1 cap is higher than legal's preferred 30% cap — we could accept it if we get one of the following commercial concessions: 
- Increase the 12-month commit discount from 10% -> 14%, or
- Add an annual minimum invoice guarantee (AMIG) for Year 1 at 95% of committed spend.

Olga — can you draft language for the emergency burst carve-out and a S1 exception to the credit cap (40% only for S1 >50%/2hr), with a commercial tie to the increased discount or AMIG? Ben/Karthik — weigh in on which concession we prefer and impact on margin. I can present back to Sara today.

Marissa
